HP Z3805A main board, Z3805-68001

The HP Z3805A main board, Z3805-68001, mapped part by part from the bench unit (serial 3625A01487, board serial 6E9008G, date code 3627, firmware 3543B; bench.md, “HP Z3805A, serial 3625A01487”). It is the first-generation SmartClock board: the Z3801A (Z3801-68001) and the 58503A (58503-60001 Rev C) use the same layout, fitted a little differently for each model, and the last two columns of the parts table say what their photos show at each designator.

Each part's firmware column cites the document and section that ties it to an address, a chip select or a QSPI device. The rings mark each part's place on the photos; select a ring to see its part, or a row to find it on the photos.

Photos 2026-10-30, board out of the chassisGPS engine module removedNets measured cold, with an ohmmeter

The marks

A ring's color is how its part is identified, its designator and marking; the table gives that and the role's apart.

  • read: read from the firmware image's code, in the cited document
  • board: seen on the board: a photo or a meter
  • inferred: inferred from what is seen or read, not checked
  • open: not known

Wheel or pinch to zoom and drag to pan; on a focused photo, + and - zoom, 0 fits and the arrows pan.

No part matches.

Part

Select a ring on the photo, or a row of the parts table, for its part.

Measured nets

Measured on the bench Z3805A on 2026-10-30, power off, with an ohmmeter, by the rules of hardware-investigations.md, “Working on the open Z3805A board”. Pin numbers are the 74ABT245A's (DIR 1, A1 to A8 2 to 9, /OE 19; ti/sn74abt245b.pdf) and the XC3042's PLCC-84.

NetPathNote
J4, OUT AJ4 center pin, through R32, to U17's B sideU17's eight outputs reach J4 through R32's eight 100 ohm resistors.
U17 A sideU17 pins 2 to 9, A1 to A8, all tied together, to U32 pin 14
J5, OUT BJ5 center pin, through R33, to U18's B sideAs J4.
U18 A sideU18 pins 2 to 9 all tied together, to U32 pin 83
DIRU17 pin 1 to R52 pin 7; U18 pin 1 to R52 pin 8; R52 pin 16, the common, to VCCPulled high, so both transfer A to B, FPGA to jack, unless something else drives the line; nothing else on it is ruled out.
/OEU17 pin 19 and U18 pin 19 joined, through one 1 kohm resistor to groundLow, so the outputs are enabled. The net runs on toward the U33 area; it is on no pin of U32 or U33. Nothing else on it is ruled out; R20 is the candidate for the resistor.

In the firmware's terms: firmware/outputs.md, “The FPGA bitstreams” decodes the Z3805A design's pin 14 as a registered, fast-slew output, where the 58503A's and Z3801A's design leaves it unregistered, and pin 45 as an output that design leaves unused. It says nothing of pin 83, or of what signal any pin carries. That J4 and J5 both carry the 1 PPS rests on their cabling to the rear panel's two 1 PPS outputs (bench.md, “HP Z3805A, serial 3625A01487”); that U32 makes the internal 1 PPS is inferred (firmware/counter.md, “Which 1 PPS edges”).

Confidence is the designator and marking's, then the role's. The last two columns compare the Z3801A's and the 58503A's boards at the same designator:

  • same: the same part as the Z3805A's, or bare on both
  • fitted: a part fitted, not compared
  • differs: fitted differently
  • open: not seen

Across the three boards

The 58503A (58503-60001 Rev C, 58503a-interior.jpg) carries the same parts at the same designators where they can be read: SCC68692C1A44 at U3, AT28C64B at U4, LT1180ACSW at U2, ADC0838CCV at U35, TLC0820AC at U36, MC144110 at U37, XC3042 at U32, and 78M12s at U45 and U46. On the Z3801A (Z3801-68001, z3801a-main-board.jpg) U4 is an Atmel part, its type under the wires, U2 an LT1180ACS, U36 a TLC0820AC, U33 an MC68331CFC16, U32 an XC3042-70 and U44 a Philips 74ABT574AD; U3 is under the add-on board.

They differ in what is fitted. U31: an empty PLCC-84 socket on the 58503A, bare pads on the Z3801A and Z3805A. U5, U6 and U7, beside the serial connector: bare on the Z3805A; on the 58503A U7 alone is fitted; on the Z3801A, whose port is RS-422 (097-z3801-01), an AT&T part sits at U5 or U6, the photo does not show which label is its. J2 and J3: boxed headers on the 58503A, bare on the Z3805A; on the Z3801A J2 is bare and a hand-wired add-on board, an MC74ACT14N on it, sits over J3. J13: on the Z3801A a bare five-position footprint beside U44, on the 58503A an AMP connector at that place; on the Z3805A the designator is printed beside U44.

The three boot two FPGA designs: the 58503A and the Z3801A share one byte for byte, and the Z3805A's differs from it at pins 14 and 45 among others (firmware/outputs.md, “The FPGA bitstreams”). The 58503A's J4 is fitted and carries no 1 PPS (hardware-investigations.md, item 19).

What the photos cannot show

Both sides are now photographed, out of the chassis. Most signal lines still change layer through vias within a few millimeters of a part's pins, so a net is followed with a meter, not by eye; only the 1 PPS output stage above has been. Not followed: the DUART's interrupt to the processor, chip select 5 to the lamp latch, the QSPI's chip-select decode, and the switch port.

U51 and U57 are under the heatsink and cannot be read without taking it off.

Open

  • Whether U32 pins 14 and 83 carry the same signal, so that J4 and J5 give the same pulse; and where pins 45 and 78 go.
  • What else is on the /OE net of U17 and U18, and whether R20 is its 1 kohm resistor; what else is on DIR.
  • The part behind the switch byte at 0x302000. Beside S1 is U21, a 74AC251, which puts one of its eight inputs on one output, not a byte on the bus; no document says what drives the byte, and S1 has not been buzzed to U21 (firmware/restart.md, “The switch byte at 0x302000”).
  • Which '138, if any, decodes chip select 5's window into the lamp latch, the switch byte, the FPGA and the EFC strobe, and what 0x306000's strobe reaches (firmware/restart.md, “The chip selects”, hardware-investigations.md, item 20).
  • What decodes the QSPI's PCS0 to PCS3 into its devices (firmware/structures.md, “The QSPI's devices”), and whether U48 and U50 take device 7's word to U56.
  • Which rail feeds U37's VDD (hardware-investigations.md, item 23); U40, a 78L12, sits beside it.
  • U51 and U57, under the heatsink.
  • Which RAM is U8 or U9 and which U15 or U16, and which pair of U11 to U14 is the lower flash bank.
  • J12: a BDM header or not (hardware-investigations.md, item 13).
  • The DUART's /INTR to U33's /IRQ2, and whether U29 is between them (hardware-investigations.md, item 21).
